from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path('src/data/lyrics/abbas-nahi-hai-wawaila.md')
_, metadata, body = path.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = []
for line in body.strip().splitlines():
    opening = re.fullmatch(r'(\\d+)\\. (.*)', line)
    if opening:
        if roman and roman[-1]:
            roman.append('')
        roman.extend(opening.groups())
    elif not (line.isdigit() or not line):
        if not roman or not roman[-1].startswith('(') or not line.startswith('('):
            roman.append(line)
        else:
            roman.append(line)

for index, line in enumerate(roman):
    for old, new in [(' maula ', ' Maula '), (' sakina ', ' Sakina '), (' zehra sani', ' Zehra Sani'), (' ali ', ' Ali '), (' shimr-e-laeen ', ' Shimr-e-laeen ')]:
        line = line.replace(old, new)
    roman[index] = line

item.text:
Reconstructed the Urdu script in [abbas-nahi-hai-wawaila.md](/home/ghayur/.local/state/kalam-codex-round2/workspaces/bd761d4163ed484cb60e20f1aa4df430/src/data/lyrics/abbas-nahi-hai-wawaila.md). The two opening lines and all nine stanzas match `romanLyrics` verse by verse. I added the Roman alternate title, set right-to-left direction, and removed `noUrdu`.

I read `Akabr` as `اکبر` and `Dekho jo` as `دیکھو جو`, preserving both readings as written in the Roman transcription.
